newsitem.title: CHINA: China official seeks state aid for wind power.
newsitem.headline: China official seeks state aid for wind power.

text.p: A Chinese energy official called on Wednesday for lower import duties and preferential loans to help speed the use of wind-generated electricity.

"Unlike the thermal power industry, China is completely dependent on imports for wind power equipment and we need some form of incentives," said Xiang Xianzhuang, deputy general manager of China Fulin Windpower Development Corp.
"We need lower import duties for equipment and low interest loans," she told Reuters at an energy conference.
China Fulin was set up by the Ministry of Power Industry to promote alternative energy sources.
China, facing growing demand for energy as its economy expands rapidly, depends overwhelmingly on coal for its electric power generation.
But the widespread use of coal-fired power plants has created major pollution problems, and economic planners are looking for ways to reduce environmental damage.

Wind power is one of several alternative forms of energy being reviewed by China but its role in the nation's energy picture is still negligible, accounting for less than one percent of total power-generating capacity.
Most wind-generated electric power in China is produced in Inner Mongolia, the far western region of Xinjiang as well as the coastal provinces of Zhejiang and Liaoning.
Xiang estimated the cost of building a wind-generated power plant in China was about double that of a thermal plant, partly because of a lack of low-price domestic equipment.
Import duties of six percent coupled with 17 percent value added tax contributed to the hefty price tag.
"Since everything is imported, import duties are a key cost factor," Xiang said. "We need to waive or reduce these duties."
Commercial loans carrying interest of about 15 percent were also putting the technology out of reach, she said.
